name: Jay Arendt
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember interpreting a consultation that needed almost no words.” Monday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Jay stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I translated her visits for sixteen years. We know each other's pauses better than some married people.
appearance: Jay has brown hair pinned away from the temples, full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, and a favorite piece of clothing, an olive canvas jacket. It usually goes with a train token tied to a zipper pull. When somebody else has the floor, Jay touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
personality: Jay enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To record the useful translation handovers.
family: Rami Bose is Jay’s second cousin. Jay chooses whether to use it. Rami saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The borrowed bass*, Rami says, “I know the old owner's favorite tune. I wrote the bass line on a grocery bag so these kids can play it when he walks into the park.”
connections: Marin Lim. Precise criticism and careful interpreting both make for better handover notes than indiscriminate praise.
